overall: The committee violated the OML by voting to extend the Superintendent's contract in executive session and by omitting the Superintendent's name from executive session notices; competence discussion, the detriment declaration, and June 7 access were not violations. No nullification, but future violations may bring it.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the committee improperly voted to extend the Superintendent's contract in executive session; the June 7 open-session vote was argued as not curing it.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee therefore violated the Open Meeting law by voting to extend the Superintendent's employment contract in executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the committee discussed the Superintendent's professional competence in executive session rather than in open session.
allegations.key_passage: However, there is no evidence in the minutes that the Committee discussed the Superintendent's professional competence even in this context.

allegations.summary: Notices for the May 25 and June 1 executive sessions said 'contract negotiations with non-union personnel' without naming the Superintendent as the person whose contract was discussed.
allegations.key_passage: The notices should have specifically stated that the Committee planned to enter executive session to conduct contract negotiations with Dr. Paul Ash.

allegations.summary: The June 7 open-meeting notice listed the Superintendent's contract only generically and did not say the committee would ratify an already-reached contract.
allegations.key_passage: the meeting notice ultimately did not provide the public with sufficient detail to understand that the Committee would be discussing a contract it had already reached in executive session and voting to ratify the contract in open session on June 7, 2011.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair failed to declare that an open meeting would be detrimental to the committee's bargaining position before entering executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the public was denied full access to the June 7 open meeting because overflow attendees in the hallway could not see or hear the proceedings.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee made reasonable efforts to ensure that all members of the public had access to the meeting, and do not believe the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law in this regard.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
